title: Targeted interventions against causal confusion
description: Learn policies over many candidate causal graphs of the input, then pick the right graph through environment interaction or expert queries.

prediction.rationale: De Haan et al.'s claim: imitation fails because the learner uses a nuisance factor that is an effect of the expert's policy, not a cause of its actions. Choosing the causal graph by intervention removes that factor, so the policy stops copying its own previous action.
